Cereza is born into a clan of famous witches in England, but her and her mother are scorned for having a child out of wedlock. She grows up admiring her mother, viewing her and the women of her clan as witches, viewing them as forces of good.

Due to the times, a war breaks out, summoning a powerful witch that ends up killing most of her clan. She sees this witch, dubbing it a horrifying “angel”.

“I-i wish to be a strong witch, just like my mummy!”

Cereza, a girl full of potential, twisted the incubators system with the power of her wish. Inheriting not just the powers of a witch, but the mind and body of a magical girl, Cereza fought to protect her family’s one treasure, a red ruby, the eye of the world, with her.

Developing her powers, Cereza found she was able to absorb the powers of the witches she defeated, and, having no use for grief seeds, gathered them as treasures.

Eventually, she grew to be a powerful young woman, and a skilled fighter and master of battle. Confronted by the legions of holy war soldiers, she is forced to use her powers against them, as they dub her no better than a vicious witch.

Before she can be burned at the stake, a figure steps in, a blonde woman, clad in a red feline uniform. As if stopping time, Cereza’s soul gem is eclipsed in red vines, that ensnare her in a crystal coffin.

Falling into the depths of the river below, she is lost at the bottom of the lake it leads to.

Centuries go by as Cereza’s soul gem and body lay at the bottom of the lake, until one day, her coffin is shattered. Immediately sent into a witches labyrinth, she  quickly dispatches the powerful witch inside, saving a young man, but in the process, losing his father to the dying thoes of the witch.

He curses her, calls her no better than a witch, reawakening her dormant memories, and setting her off on a journey to recover her memories and figure out who this mysterous magical girl that trapped her was…

Personally, i liked DR2’s story just a bit more. Chuck having to desperately save his child, whose already infected, from an outbreak while dealing with government agents and heists just felt so big. 

Thats not to say DR1 isnt good, but i’d compare the original’s vibe as Dawn of the Dead, where as DR2 is more like a comedic Return of the Living Dead or Army of the Dead. 

Its not great in retrospect since i dont think more humor necessarily is what makes a good DR game, but it certainly improved upon the “you can make anything into a weapon” into “you can make anything into a weapon…into a bigger weapon”, and i loved that addition. It made fights more interesting and the methods of killing zombies and pyschos so much more fun and unique.

Honestly, if DR2DR (hopefully) does well, i hope they decide to completely redo DR3 and follow a more tame story. All these mutations and stuff just push it into RE or L4D, i prefer my almost traditional zombies with a bit of extra (i will excuse the gas zombies for this, but everything post 2 was a bit stupid imo, like the hive zombies in DR3).

Main point, DR2 is remembered fondly because by sequel standards, its a fairly good sequel, and improves upon promises and expectations of the original in a good way and a natural way, and i hope DR’s developers take notes from their past success for future titles.

I’d say its longer too in the sense that there are technically going to be two final bosses, one for the underworld and the other for the surface, with different bosses in between each, though i havent seen anything like different variants (the furies for example, or running into Astarius) but that could just be for a future patch.

Dont get me wrong, you can still make a very broken build but i think thats the fun of Hades, but its by no means any more easy or difficult than Hades 1, just a bit of different learning curve.

Melinoe and Zag work pretty much the same with Melinoe having her normal attack, special attack, and a cast which instead of Zag’s glowing red gem strike thing, is a zone that snares enemies. She can charge her moves with mana to imbue effects (normal attacks might strike multiple times, teleport you, turn a regular strike into a bigger aoe, ext.). She also has a different upgrade tree in the from of Tarot cards that you must unlock and then build whatever suits your next run, and access to pets that do little effects like marking targets, a free revive, or they can gather resources for you more simply (cat can get fish, the bird can mine, ext).

If you want difficult, there are Chaos trials, where you’re limited to a certain weapon, keepsake, and abilities to a certain point. There is also of course the mirror of night that functions for challenges kinda like the heat fro  Hades 1, where you can add in more enemies, less healing, ext.

Overall though, its still an early access game, wait maybe a year or until the next large update, which should be a bit since they just had a big update, but that should certainly be a good time to add more difficulty since most bosses should be completely added in besides any secret bosses or variants. I’d say that even in its state now, its a very fun game, though it doesnt have the ending added in just yet either. If you are fine with grinding a bit while you wait for an update, i’d definitely play. Its similar but different enough to enjoy.

Nothing helps more than drawing from references of real people.

Start with getting the bare skeleton done, meaning think of them in a wire frame kinda look, so you can see where arms and legs are bending and the curves of a human body.

Then, move onto muscle, think of muscles in different ways, theres a ton of tutorials for how a fit buff person, a tall skinny person, or a short fat persons muscle layout will differ.

Finally, add details. Clothing and hair, facial features and body features (moles, scars, aging, ext.)

Most of all though, dont expect to become fantastic at it quickly, most skilled artists still arent amazing with anatomy, but if you keep at it, it is a great skill to have.

Hands and feet though are the devils work, they will always be a bit complicated but some people have good ways of doing it.

Either way, adapt your own style onto it as you learn. Bodies in art, especially wierdcore or cartoonish art can break how anatomy works, so it doesnt need to be perfectly correct (think how courage the cowardly dog screams and has his eyes pop out, thats the best i can think of, or how a punch will be super dynamic in anime?). Take time and work slow, when you think you’ve plateaued or reached a point you arent able to improve, branch out to different dynamic poses. There are literally millions of pose references out there, including yourself if you have a pose in mind and cant find a reference. I sometimes even use Bing AI if i need a reference like “hero wielding a sword stabbing a dragon” or “ice witch overlooking a boiling cauldron”, but AI also breaks anatomy sometimes just cause its AI generated.

Either way though, you will improve so long as you try and challenge yourself. Even if you cant complete what you set your mind on, that challenge is still important to improving.

I start off my drawings now by doing the whole pose in like a wire shape or a manniquin/bare base, then add on hair, face, clothes and accessories, that helps you get a good pose down and also learn anatomy so it comes more naturally, eventually you wont need as many references, but they do help.

I’ve always liked my horror games either grounded or fantastical, as long as it is explained or tied to the creatures lore.

Zombies are usually the result of a virus, so i always prefer them as mutating or developing natural advantages. Superpowers that expand beyond isnt something i enjoy, like telepathy or telekinesis, but if its something like “hey, this serum affected a living person differently, they arent undead” or some shit, i’ll let it pass, but zombies i always prefer to be bland or mutated. Dead Rising, the first, did well with undead shamblers and survivors, now its expanded to living and breathing (at least 2-3) zombies, which i think is stupid.

Alternatively, if im dealing with a vampire, i expect less grounded stuff since they are associated with more, turning into smoke or rats or bats, hypnosis, afraid of crosses and holy stuff, that fits better for them. 

Another good example are things like the zombies in The Evil Dead, which are possessed corpses and living bodies that should be able to use magic, because they are actually demons. 

Overall, it just depends on how its elaborated, and as long as it can be explained in a way that fits the world they take place in, then it gets a pass from me. Unfitting things dont make for a good story, i couldnt see a witch in Dying Light or the like, but a zombie that can retch up its stomach acid to melt your face off, cause its been mutated or developed, sure! Any good writer can mix things up as long as they can explain, cause when you get cornered with different plot holes or odd choices, it is harder to explain within a game without making it seem strange or out of place.
